question: Does cycling the coupling of a pairwise isotropic Gaussian-Markov random field produce an asymmetric relationship between a proposed parameter-manifold curvature and conditional entropy?

key_findings.claim: For a three-parameter pairwise isotropic Gaussian-Markov random field, the paper writes first- and second-order Fisher-information matrices from local conditional moments and defines a shape operator P=-II I^{-1}.
key_findings.evidence: Equations 2-11 express matrix entries through variance and neighborhood covariances; determinant, trace, and eigenvalues of P are then called Gaussian, mean, and principal curvatures.

key_findings.claim: A 1,000-step Metropolis-Hastings cycle ramps inverse temperature beta from zero by 0.0006 for 500 steps and then reverses it, while estimating mean, variance, covariances, entropy, and curvature along the path.
key_findings.evidence: The simulation protocol fixes an isotropic second-order neighborhood, increases beta deterministically in the first half, decreases it in the second, and re-estimates mu and sigma squared from samples.

key_findings.claim: In the displayed run, Gaussian curvature changes sign near sharp entropy changes, and the curvature excursion is substantially larger on the decreasing-entropy return path than on the increasing-entropy path.
key_findings.evidence: Figures 2-4 plot Gaussian curvature, mean curvature, and the conditional-entropy expression over the cycle; the text names their path asymmetry the curvature effect.

key_findings.claim: Plotting entropy against Gaussian curvature gives a loop that resembles hysteresis, which the paper interprets as irreversible parameter-space deformation and an intrinsic arrow of time.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 5 compares the outward and return branches and the conclusion says the curvature required for the entropy-decreasing branch is larger than for the same-magnitude increase.

key_findings.claim: The protocol-induced loop does not establish an intrinsic arrow of time: beta is externally ramped while a finite MCMC chain may lag equilibrium, and no quasistatic-rate, reverse-initialization, equilibration, or uncertainty study separates genuine hysteresis from relaxation bias.
key_findings.evidence: Only one fixed 1,000-step schedule is described, with no lattice size, burn-in, mixing diagnostic, replicate, error bar, or ramp-rate scaling reported in the paper.

key_findings.claim: Calling the second-order Fisher matrix a second fundamental form and its derived determinant a Gaussian curvature requires an embedding/extrinsic-geometric justification that is not supplied; intrinsic information geometry normally derives curvature from the Fisher metric and its connection.
key_findings.evidence: The manuscript asserts II as a second fundamental form and directly sets P=-II I^{-1} without specifying an ambient embedding, normal field, Gauss-Codazzi compatibility, or comparison with the Riemann curvature tensor of I.

method.core_idea: Track a proposed extrinsic curvature of the statistical parameter space of a spatial Gaussian model while its coupling parameter is cycled, and compare curvature with entropy.
method.mechanism: Represent the field through local Gaussian conditional densities with parameters (mu, sigma squared, beta), estimate neighborhood covariances during Metropolis-Hastings sampling, populate two Fisher-derived matrices, compute P=-II I^{-1}, and plot determinant/trace/eigenvalues and conditional entropy as beta rises and falls.
assumptions: The field is Markovian, Gaussian, pairwise, isotropic, stationary, and described by one spatially constant coupling beta.
Local conditional moments adequately represent the relevant joint statistical manifold and entropy.
The proposed second-order Fisher matrix is a legitimate second fundamental form compatible with the Fisher metric.
The finite MCMC state at each beta approximates the intended equilibrium distribution.
A single driven cycle can distinguish intrinsic irreversibility from schedule-dependent sampling lag.

techniques.role: Avoids the full Gibbs normalizer by specifying local pairwise conditionals.
Defines the reported Gaussian, mean, and principal curvature signals.
Drives the field from independence to stronger coupling and back.
Visualizes directional asymmetry and the proposed hysteresis effect.

evaluations.setting: One two-dimensional pairwise isotropic GMRF MCMC cycle
evaluations.metric: Gaussian/mean curvature and conditional entropy over 1,000 beta updates
evaluations.result: Curvature changes sign near sharp entropy changes and the return branch has a larger magnitude than the outward branch in the displayed trajectory.
evaluations.baseline: The beta=0 independent Gaussian geometry and comparison of increasing versus decreasing beta branches

evaluations.result: The curve resembles hysteresis and is interpreted as a curvature effect, but no equilibrium or replicate baseline quantifies the loop area or uncertainty.

limitations: Only one highly restricted Gaussian pairwise isotropic field and one coupling schedule are studied.
Lattice size, burn-in, autocorrelation, mixing, independent repetitions, numerical uncertainty, and finite-size scaling are not reported.
The entropy formula is based on local conditional structure and is not validated against the normalized joint-field entropy.
The extrinsic second-form/shape-operator construction is asserted rather than geometrically derived in this paper.
No conventional order parameter, susceptibility, correlation length, or independently established critical point validates the claimed phase transitions.
failure_modes: Slow mixing under the beta ramp produces an artificial loop even for an equilibrium-reversible model.
Near-singularity of the estimated Fisher matrix makes P and its determinant numerically unstable.
Finite-sample covariance error changes curvature sign without a thermodynamic transition.
Conditional/pseudolikelihood entropy moves differently from the true joint entropy.
An arbitrary redefinition of the second form changes the claimed extrinsic curvature and arrow of time.
reusable_insights: For driven phase-transition diagnostics, sweep rate toward zero, reverse the schedule, vary initialization, and report loop-area finite-size scaling.
Compare any proposed curvature with an intrinsic Fisher-Riemann scalar and with standard critical observables.
Propagate Monte Carlo autocorrelation and covariance-estimation uncertainty through matrix inversion and curvature.
Distinguish equilibrium state-space geometry from nonequilibrium path dependence before claiming irreversibility.
open_questions: Does the curvature loop persist after full equilibration at each beta and vanish or remain under quasistatic driving?
Is the proposed shape operator compatible with an explicit embedding of the GMRF family?
How does the signal scale with lattice size and align with correlation-length or susceptibility critical points?
Does joint-likelihood entropy reproduce the local-conditional entropy relationship?
Can the effect be reproduced in Ising, Potts, anisotropic, non-Gaussian, or higher-order fields with uncertainty bars?

competitive_landscape.title: On the curvatures of Gaussian random field manifolds
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct predecessor by the same author
competitive_landscape.difference: The predecessor derives the same Fisher-based curvature expressions and notes sign/asymmetry; this short paper foregrounds the entropy-curvature hysteresis loop and intrinsic-time interpretation rather than introducing an independently validated geometry.

competitive_landscape.title: Thermodynamic curvature: pure fluids to black holes
competitive_landscape.difference: Ruppeiner curvature is an invariant scalar of a thermodynamic information metric with links to fluctuation length; this work uses an asserted extrinsic shape operator of a conditional GMRF parameterization and interprets a driven trajectory.

competitive_landscape.title: Thermodynamic Geometry, Phase Transitions, and the Widom Line
competitive_landscape.difference: Ruppeiner et al. compare scalar-curvature coexistence/Widom predictions with fluid data; the curvature-effect letter supplies one simulation trace without thermodynamic or experimental calibration.

competitive_landscape.title: Detecting Quantum and Classical Phase Transitions via Unsupervised Machine Learning of the Fisher Information Metric
competitive_landscape.difference: ClassiFIM estimates the Fisher metric from limited samples and quantitatively benchmarks transition localization across many classical/quantum models; this paper analytically parameterizes one GMRF and does not test detection accuracy.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: An asymmetric entropy-curvature hysteresis in a Gaussian random-field manifold reveals a new curvature effect and an intrinsic arrow of time.
novelty_assessment.evidence: A single beta-up/beta-down MCMC trajectory shows different reported curvature magnitudes for matched entropy changes and a loop in entropy-versus-curvature space.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The plotted asymmetry is a hypothesis-generating observation, not yet a demonstrated intrinsic effect. The proposed geometry needs independent derivation, and the simulation must rule out finite-chain/ramp hysteresis before supporting phase-transition or arrow-of-time claims.

reviewer_notes: Read all 5 extracted pages, checking the conditional model, both Fisher-derived matrices, entropy formula, exact beta schedule, figures, and conclusion. Direct predecessor, thermodynamic-geometry, and later Fisher-metric phase-detection papers were checked on arXiv on 2026-08-23.
